steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Human language has unique features (Hockett's design features): semanticity (words have meaning), generativity (can create infinite new sentences), displacement (can talk about past/future/abstract), arbitrariness (no connection between word and referent), and cultural transmission (learned from others).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Animal communication: bees use waggle dances to communicate food location (shows displacement and semanticity but not generativity). Vervet monkeys use distinct alarm calls for different predators (shows semanticity but limited generativity). Birdsongs are largely innate with some learned elements.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Washoe the chimp: taught over 100 signs in ASL, combined signs creatively (e.g. 'water bird' for swan). However, critics argued Washoe's signing was operant conditioning rather than true language - she didn't use syntax consistently.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Kanzi the bonobo: learned lexigram symbols through observation (not explicit training). Kanzi understood spoken English and could follow complex instructions. Showed some understanding of word order, suggesting rudimentary syntax.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Human language = generativity + displacement + syntax. Animal communication = limited, fixed signals. Washoe = chimp learned ASL. Kanzi = bonobo learned lexigrams. Alex = parrot learned English words. When evaluating animal language studies, consider: is it true language or operant conditioning? Are researchers over-interpreting?
